caveat: This is a qualified comparison of binding texts, not a court finding. Directive-consistent interpretation and EU rights may narrow the effect. resolution: The current official registry identifies the 2026 rule as valid from 14 June 2026 and lists only its original version. No later binding correction resolving this fruit-name discrepancy was located.

title: The new jam rules keep pomegranates where the EU amendment specifies cashew apples
summary: Slovenia raised its jam quantities in 2026 but retained “granatna jabolka” (pomegranates) in the special fruit category. The replacing EU text expressly uses “akažujeva jabolka” (cashew apples).
nationalGap: The new national Annex 1 points 1–2 retain the old Slovenian EU term for pomegranates, although the authentic 2024 replacement uses cashew apples. Articles 2 and 4 make the national annex operative. The EU-reference clause in Article 1 does not itself rewrite that table.
nationalLaw: Pravilnik o kakovosti in označevanju sadnih džemov, želejev, marmelad in sladkane kostanjeve kaše, SOP 2026-01-0809, Articles 1–7 and Annex 1 points 1–2.
consequence: On the written national categories, pomegranate jam could use the special 230 g minimum rather than the EU general 450 g; extra jam could use 290 g rather than 500 g. Cashew apples could instead face the national general minima. These are potential recipe consequences; no actual product or enforcement outcome was established.
review: The parent and a verification researcher independently read the whole six-page national rule, including all three annexes, and the authentic Slovenian original and replacing EU texts. The verifier separately checked the current official registry. Official Slovenian phytosanitary guidance independently identifies granatno jabolko as Punica granatum (pomegranate).
recognitionNote: Bounded Slovenian and English searches on 27 October 2026 combined the two fruit names, the national rule identifier and the EU amendment. They found the legislation and general reform material, but no precise prior criticism of this retained fruit-name mismatch. This does not establish first discovery.

comparison.after: 230 g / 290 g for akažujeva jabolka (cashew apples).
comparison.note: General minima are 450 g for jam and 500 g for extra jam. The comparison concerns new goods outside the earlier-stock protection.
